name: Systems Blueprint
summary: One persistent diagram of a system that the film lights up part by part: a signal travels the path, a part fails, the consequence spreads. For software, networks, infrastructure and machines.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: Trace what happens from input to output and name the part that fails or limits the system.
visual_job.hero: One diagram drawn once, whose parts change state (light, dim, fill) instead of being replaced.

use_when: The point is how parts connect, pass data or fail.
A process has stages, actors or a causal chain.
The subject is a system the viewer cannot see: software, networks, infrastructure, machines.
avoid_when: The point is a number or its trend (use data-ledger).
The piece derives or proves something (use proof-canvas).
The story is about people rather than parts (use storybook).

alternates.when: Type-led film with very few objects.
The brief asks for a dark technical look.

scene_grammar.formula: The hero object on screen from frame 1, then the question it raises.
Draw the whole system once, small and labelled. This is the diagram the rest of the film reuses.
A packet or token travels the path; one stage is lit at a time, the rest dimmed.
Break or overload one part and show the consequence propagate along the connectors.
The same diagram under load or at scale: copies, counters, a changed colour state.
The diagram returns collapsed to the one idea, in the state it started in or resolved to (bookend).

motion.signature: A persistent diagram: parts are drawn once, then change state rather than being swapped for a new graphic per sentence.
motion.continuous_layer: Slow scale or pan on the diagram group for the whole scene, plus a travelling signal on the active path.
avoid: Labels that appear without a connector to their part.
Decorative particles that carry no data.

rules.ending: Bookend: return to the opening object in its resolved state; land the last sound on the last visual event; tail after the last word 2-3 s.

anti_patterns.pattern: Narration over a frame that does not change for more than max_beat_gap_sec.
anti_patterns.why: Breaks the anti-laziness rule. motion-qa flagged 41 s of 70 (cloud), 44 s of 92 (fridge), 79 s of 98 (Korea) as static or low-energy. Plan one visual event per 2-3 s from measured onsets and give every scene a drift layer (Studio.space.drift).

anti_patterns.pattern: Labels below the type floor (2.6% of the short side) to fit more on screen.
anti_patterns.why: Cloud had 21 text-size-floor warnings at 12.5-17 px and still shipped at readability 3. Cut the label or split the beat; never shrink the type.

anti_patterns.pattern: Leader lines or tags that touch other text or sit on their own node.
anti_patterns.why: Fridge's dotted leader ran through 'ONLINE'; cloud's 'DELHI' tag sat on its node; a phone touched a kicker. No check catches this; open the full-size frame at each scene's first and last beat.

anti_patterns.pattern: A headline that restates the narration.
anti_patterns.why: Fridge headlines repeated 82-83% of the voice, which wastes the strongest text slot. Use it for what the voice does not say (the number, the contrast, the date). A caption band is a legitimate repeat.

anti_patterns.pattern: Over-budget narration in the hook and closing scenes.
anti_patterns.why: They are written last. Cloud's s1 and s6 ran 35-36 words per 10 s against a 33 budget and the film read rushed. Cut words; do not raise the speed.

reference_projects.note: Legacy technical explainer; the subject type this template targets.
Mechanism film whose review produced most of the anti-patterns above.

open_questions: dark-tech is experimental and was used by polya-recurrence; decide whether this template needs a documented dark mode or leaves dark to proof-canvas.

revisions.change: Initial version. Rules taken from the neutral-technical narration budget (30 words per 10 s) and the 2026-11-03 review of the three newest films.
